title: Interactions Protect Periodically Driven Time Crystals Against Dephasing but Destabilise Multipolar-Driven Order
abstract: We show that stronger interactions protect periodically driven time-crystal order against dephasing but destabilise order under random multipolar drives, and that coordination matters beyond the total interaction strength. We studied a disordered kicked Ising model of $N=12$ and $16$ spins with imperfect $π$ pulses and per-site dephasing by exact diagonalisation, comparing a periodic drive, random multipolar drives of order $n=0,1,2$ and the Thue-Morse sequence, and separated coupling strength from coordination by comparing a grid with a ring at equal total interaction strength $zJ$. For the periodic drive the coherence time scales approximately as $1/γ$, and stronger coupling reduces the transverse tilt on which dephasing acts. For multipolar drives of order $n\ge1$, doubling the coupling on a ring shortens the coherence time to $0.54$ ($n=1$), $0.37$ ($n=2$) and $0.44$ (Thue-Morse) at $N=16$, while random signs ($n=0$) are unaffected. A disorder scan supports a toggling-frame picture in which interactions spoil the block cancellation of the pulse error. At equal $zJ$ the grid outlives the ring by $2.15$ ($N=12$) and $2.78$ ($N=16$) for the periodic drive despite an identical transverse tilt, a coordination effect beyond this picture. All ratios hold under three definitions of the coherence time.
summary: This paper analyzes the stability of time-crystal order in a disordered kicked Ising model under various driving protocols. It finds that interactions offer protection against dephasing for periodic drives but destabilize multipolar drives, while also revealing a geometry-dependent 'coordination gain' not predicted by simple tilt measurements. The findings advance understanding of decoherence mechanisms in periodically driven quantum matter.
main_problem: The study investigates how different types of interactions affect the coherence time of time-crystal order in periodically driven quantum systems, particularly comparing periodic versus random multipolar drives.
main_result: Stronger interactions protect time-crystal order against dephasing from periodic drives but destabilize it under random multipolar drives, and coordination effects beyond total interaction strength are measurable.
method: The research employs exact diagonalization (ED) simulations and Matrix-Product-State (MPS) time evolution to analyze the dynamics of a disordered kicked Ising model.
model_or_system: The system is a disordered kicked Ising model of spin-1/2 sites, driven by periodic or random multipolar sequences, and subjected to per-site dephasing ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Coherence time ($T_c$), transverse tilt ($	heta^2_\perp$), and ratios of coherence times across different drive types and lattice geometries.
important_parameters: The disorder strength ($D$), the coupling strength ($J$), the dephasing rate ($\gamma$), and the drive order ($n=0, 1, 2$).
main_assumptions: The initial state is assumed to be fully polarized; the coherence time definition is sensitive, requiring multiple checks for robustness.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the periodic tilt, block residuals, and measured ratios of coherence times for $N=16$, while tables show disorder scan results for $T_c$ ratios.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the coherence time scaling for periodic drives versus multipolar drives, analyzes the role of geometry (grid vs. ring) at fixed interaction strength, and discusses the underlying 'toggling-frame' picture.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed insights into how local disorder and structured interactions compete with environmental decoherence in non-equilibrium quantum many-body systems, which is highly relevant to understanding quantum computation stability.
